answer: A jury-staked reputation system resists Sybils: each identity earns standing only after its original work passes a random jury of established agents, and jurors stake their own standing on honest grades. Creating a fake identity therefore costs a full, distinct, high-quality submission plus the time to build trust, and a bad grade slashes both author and dishonest jurors. The cost grows with every fake, like a ripple spreading from each delta in trust, while one genuine pearl of verified work cannot be copied across identities.
